title: Regulated Prediction-Market Terminals & Licensed iGaming Affiliates — Operator Companion Workbook
subtitle: 6 Printable Operator Worksheets for Non-Custodial Event-Contract Analytics, Licensed Affiliate Underwriting, CPA/NGR Economics, Jurisdiction Controls, Reliable Attribution, and Small-Team Launch

worksheets.title: Arbitrage Deal / Counterparty Underwriting & Spread Qualification
worksheets.purpose: Qualify the information advantage before spending acquisition capital. Separate subscription analytics, permitted builder payments, and licensed affiliate commissions; assess counterparties, settlement terms, and geographic eligibility. Treat every worked example as an illustrative underwriting case, not evidence of current permission or an executable trading opportunity.
instructions: Create three separate commercial lanes: analytics subscriptions, permitted builder payments, and licensed affiliate commissions. Identify the payer, earned event, collection timetable, and registration dependency for each; reject any arrangement requiring customer balances, pooled capital, or access to customer trading credentials.

Read the actual counterparty agreement and current regulator records before assigning a permission status. Record the entity, jurisdiction, product, verification date, and reviewer; a recognized brand or accessible API does not establish that every proposed activity is permitted.

Normalize contracts by settlement event, expiration, cancellation rules, fees, and executable size before calculating a spread. Keep event-contract probabilities separate from sportsbook implied probabilities unless the comparison clearly explains the different payout mechanics and outcome coverage.

Request commission statements covering both peak football months and quieter periods. Rebuild approved first-time depositor counts, contractual deductions, reversals, and negative carryover from transaction evidence; headline CPA rates alone cannot support a defensible acquisition budget or revenue forecast.

Assign a written accept, revise, or reject decision to each proposed relationship. Attach the supporting evidence and the next review date; unresolved licensing, settlement, or payment questions must stop the affected commercial lane without stopping independently qualified subscription work.

fields.name: Commercial lane and earned-revenue event
fields.prompt: Describe exactly what the business sells, who pays, and which event earns each payment. Distinguish recurring software access from approved referrals and net affiliate commissions; exclude all customer deposits and trading turnover.
fields.example: The illustrative base plan earns $180,000 from analytics subscriptions, $12,500 from contractually permitted builder payments, $120,000 from approved CPA referrals, and $50,000 from NGR commissions. Total operator revenue is $362,500. Customer stakes, deposits, contract notional, and sportsbook handle never enter these four revenue accounts.

fields.name: Counterparty identity and permission evidence
fields.prompt: Record the contracting legal entity, regulator record, covered product, geographic scope, and agreement signatory. Explain how the reviewer will establish that the specific entity can offer the proposed product to the targeted audience.
fields.example: Before contracting with a Kalshi-linked software program, the reviewer captures the relevant CFTC designation record and the program's written eligibility terms. A New Jersey sportsbook relationship receives separate NJ DGE verification. The evidence packet identifies both legal entities and does not transfer permission between unrelated products.

fields.name: Publisher versus intermediary activity boundary
fields.prompt: List every proposed user interaction involving recommendations, account opening, orders, compensation, or credentials. Identify facts requiring an IB, FCM, or CTA analysis instead of assuming that non-custodial software automatically qualifies as an excluded publisher.
fields.example: Version one displays research and sends user-configured alerts; it does not accept orders, obtain trading keys, transmit instructions, or hold money. Counsel evaluates 7 U.S.C. 1a(12), 1a(28), 1a(31), and 6d before adding compensated solicitation, individualized recommendations, or an account-opening integration. The operating description is attached to that review.

fields.name: Settlement-equivalence comparison
fields.prompt: Specify the event, authoritative settlement source, outcome coverage, expiration, cancellation treatment, and payout unit for both instruments. Explain any difference that prevents a displayed probability gap from representing an economically matched comparison.
fields.example: Two election contracts reference different certification deadlines: one settles after state certification and the other after final electoral certification. A displayed four-point gap is therefore classified as a settlement-basis difference, not a locked spread. The terminal retains both rule excerpts and suppresses its matched-contract comparison badge.

fields.name: Executable spread and fee qualification
fields.prompt: Calculate a matched hypothetical spread using executable prices, contract size, fees, and adverse-fill allowances. State the assumptions needed for complementary payouts, and distinguish an informational calculation from an order-execution service or promised customer return.
fields.example: For genuinely complementary $1 payouts, illustrative purchase prices of $0.46 and $0.49 total $0.95. Allowing $0.02 combined fees and $0.01 slippage leaves $0.02 per pair, or $20 across 1,000 pairs. The display marks simultaneous execution, available depth, settlement equivalence, and venue access as unconfirmed until separately evidenced.

fields.name: Market-data rights and freshness
fields.prompt: Document the source, permitted display and redistribution rights, timestamp semantics, rate limits, and stale-data threshold. Explain how the product behaves when a venue offers polling rather than a permitted streaming connection for the required data.
fields.example: The ingestion plan uses a Kalshi WebSocket connection only within documented access rights. ForecastEx and sportsbook data require separately confirmed licensed delivery arrangements; streaming availability is not assumed. Quotes older than 1,500 milliseconds receive a stale flag, and the terminal stops actionable comparisons until fresh sequence continuity returns.

fields.name: CPA qualification and rejection schedule
fields.prompt: Define a qualifying first-time depositor, eligible territory, age condition, minimum deposit, attribution window, and disallowed traffic. Calculate approved revenue after rejections instead of multiplying every submitted registration by the advertised headline CPA.
fields.example: The sample agreement pays $300 per approved first-time depositor within a 30-day attribution window. Of 500 submitted events, 400 qualify and 100 fail documented eligibility or duplication checks. Recognized CPA revenue is 400 multiplied by $300, or $120,000; the rejected events contribute no commission.

fields.name: NGR definition and deduction waterfall
fields.prompt: Transcribe the contractual NGR formula, deduction categories, revenue-share percentage, negative-carryover basis, and cross-product netting rules. Reconcile operator-supplied statements to this definition before treating any reported gaming amount as earned affiliate revenue.
fields.example: The base illustration starts with $300,000 attributable GGR, subtracts $60,000 bonuses, $25,000 permitted tax deductions, and $15,000 administration charges, producing $200,000 eligible NGR. A 25% share earns $50,000. There is no opening deficit in this case; neither GGR nor eligible NGR is operator revenue.

fields.name: Seasonality and counterparty concentration
fields.prompt: Map expected approved referrals by season and payer. Stress changes in CPA prices, monthly acquisition caps, payment timing, and single-counterparty concentration; identify the first budget reduction that preserves subscription service when affiliate demand weakens.
fields.example: The 400 approved base referrals comprise 240 during four peak months and 160 during eight quieter months. A downside case cuts quiet-month approvals to 80, reducing CPA revenue from $120,000 to $96,000 at an unchanged $300 rate. The founder reduces affiliate acquisition spending before cutting subscription support capacity.

fields.name: Underwriting decision and stop conditions
fields.prompt: Record the relationship decision, responsible reviewer, required evidence, next review date, and explicit conditions that suspend promotion. Distinguish a commercial concern from a statutory restriction so operators know which remediation can reopen activity.
fields.example: Decision: revise the sample NGR agreement before launch because administration deductions lack a contractual cap. The founder requests a defined schedule and audit rights within ten business days. Promotion remains disabled if territorial authorization lapses, the counterparty changes its licensed entity, or an invoice exceeds its agreed payment deadline.

worksheets.completion_gate: Advance only when every proposed revenue lane has a documented payer, earned event, permission analysis, fee or deduction schedule, collection term, and named owner. Suspend unresolved relationships while retaining independently qualified work.

worksheets.title: Unit Economics, Escrow/Reserve Float & Working-Capital Calculator
worksheets.purpose: Reconcile the canonical scorecard to earned operator revenue and cash requirements without importing customer funds. Model subscription contribution, approved CPA economics, net NGR payments, collection delays, and business-owned reserves. Keep restricted cash, expense recognition, owner draws, and revenue deductions in separate calculations.
instructions: Copy all three canonical scenarios exactly before adding sensitivity cases. Their revenue, profit, margin, and team figures are fixed planning anchors; a revised assumption belongs in a separately labeled stress case rather than silently replacing the published base economics.

Reconstruct annual revenue from subscription service periods, approved builder entitlements, accepted CPA events, and contractually calculated NGR shares. Document the principal-versus-agent assessment under ASC 606 where applicable; underlying customer activity never becomes revenue merely because a dashboard displays it.

Assign acquisition and delivery costs to their actual commercial lanes before calculating contribution. Include rejected affiliate events, support labor, market-data fees, payment processing, refunds, and expected collection losses; avoid counting contractual NGR deductions twice as both revenue reductions and operating expenses.

Build a weekly cash schedule using contractual payment dates and realistic dispute delays. Treat business-owned cash reserves as liquidity allocations, not automatic expenses; any escrow contemplated here holds only the company's money and never customer trading or gambling balances.

Run independent stresses for off-season referral volume, commission rate reductions, negative carryover, and slower collections. Identify the minimum free-cash floor and specific spending response, then reconcile opening cash, receipts, payments, restricted transfers, and closing available cash.

fields.name: Conservative canonical reconciliation
fields.prompt: Enter the conservative revenue bridge, total operating costs, annual owner net profit, margin, and staffing. Show arithmetic that preserves the canonical figures while keeping each earned-revenue lane separate from customer economic activity.
fields.example: Conservative revenue is $45,000 SaaS, $5,000 builder payments, $20,000 CPA, and $5,000 NGR commissions, totaling $75,000. Costs are $55,500, leaving $19,500 annual owner net profit. The margin is 26%, and staffing remains one full-time operator plus two contractors. This bridge is illustrative; the scorecard totals are fixed.

fields.name: Base-case canonical reconciliation
fields.prompt: Reconcile the base scenario by revenue lane and expense category. State whether modeled full-time compensation is already included, and keep owner distributions separate so cash withdrawals do not accidentally reduce operating profit twice.
fields.example: Base revenue totals $362,500. Expenses are $96,000 full-time compensation, $48,000 contractors, $36,000 CAC, $18,000 infrastructure, $12,000 legal work, $6,750 business software, and $8,000 expected collection losses. Total costs are $224,750; owner net profit is $137,750 at 38.0%, after modeled compensation, with one full-time operator and two contractors.

fields.name: Scaled canonical reconciliation
fields.prompt: Enter scaled annual revenue, costs, profit, and headcount without equating higher customer activity with higher recognized revenue. Explain the operational assumptions that support improved margin rather than merely increasing the margin percentage.
fields.example: Scaled revenue is $300,000 SaaS, $25,000 builder payments, $225,000 CPA, and $100,000 NGR commissions, totaling $650,000. Costs total $325,000, leaving $325,000 owner net profit at 50%. Staffing is two full-time operators plus three contractors, five people overall; shared ingestion and statement automation support the margin improvement.

fields.name: Subscription and builder contribution
fields.prompt: Calculate subscription revenue from paid service months and earned pricing, then identify allocated delivery costs. Record builder payments separately with their contractual earning conditions; distinguish deferred subscription cash from revenue already earned.
fields.example: The base subscription plan contains 3,600 paid subscriber-months at $50, producing $180,000 annual revenue. Allocating $18,000 infrastructure and $9,000 CAC leaves $153,000 before labor and shared expenses. Builder revenue adds $12,500 only after qualifying terms are satisfied. An annual prepayment is recognized over its service period.

fields.name: CPA cohort contribution after acquisition
fields.prompt: Compute acquisition cost per submitted and approved referral, earned CPA revenue, and contribution before shared expenses. Reconcile this lane's acquisition allocation to the company total and describe how reversals change the cohort.
fields.example: Affiliate CPA acquisition consumes $24,000 of the $36,000 base CAC budget. Five hundred submitted events cost $48 each; 400 approvals cost $60 each. At $300 per approval, revenue is $120,000 and contribution is $96,000 before labor and shared costs. The remaining CAC allocation is $9,000 SaaS and $3,000 NGR.

fields.name: NGR retained share and negative carryover
fields.prompt: Calculate the affiliate's retained commission after contractual deductions and opening deficits. Specify whether carryover is measured before or after the revenue-share percentage, and explain how that convention affects the next payable statement.
fields.example: Base eligible NGR of $200,000 multiplied by retained_share of 0.25 earns $50,000. In a separate stress example, a $12,000 pre-share deficit offsets the next month's $28,000 positive NGR, leaving $16,000 and a $4,000 commission. The deficit is not deducted again after the 25% calculation or booked as company GMV.

fields.name: Business reserve and customer-fund exclusion
fields.prompt: Identify unrestricted operating cash, company-owned restricted reserves, expected collection-loss expense, and any contractual escrow. Explain the accounting and access differences; no worksheet entry may authorize holding user deposits or wagering balances.
fields.example: The founder allocates $10,000 of company cash to a separate reversal reserve account. This transfer reduces freely deployable liquidity but does not itself create an expense. The base model's $8,000 expected collection-loss expense requires separate accounting support. Customer deposits remain entirely with the licensed venue, outside company accounts and ledgers.

fields.name: Working-capital requirement and collection delay
fields.prompt: Estimate the affiliate cash gap from recognized commissions, contractual collection time, payable timing, and available liquidity. Separate the receivable balance from the operating funding requirement, and show a practical response to delayed settlement.
fields.example: Base CPA plus NGR revenue is $170,000 annually, approximately $14,166.67 monthly. At 60-day collection timing, average affiliate receivables are roughly $28,333.33 before disputes. This receivable estimate is not itself required funding. A weekly cash forecast determines the gap; the founder pauses discretionary ads if available cash falls below $15,000.

fields.name: Startup capital and operating-cost scope
fields.prompt: Allocate startup capital within the canonical range and define which costs the quoted monthly operating range includes. Reconcile that narrower infrastructure budget with the larger fully loaded annual scorecard expense base.
fields.example: A $35,000 startup allocation funds $10,000 product work, $8,000 legal and registration work, $4,000 data setup, and $13,000 working capital. It fits the $8,000–$45,000 range. The $1,500–$10,000 monthly opex range describes an operating envelope, not every fully loaded scenario; base annual costs of $224,750 average $18,729.17 monthly.

fields.name: Downside profit and cash response
fields.prompt: Calculate a clearly labeled downside case without changing canonical scorecard figures. Include reduced affiliate approvals and an explicit expense response; state which assumptions remain unchanged and how much owner net profit survives.
fields.example: The seasonality stress removes 80 approved referrals at $300, reducing base revenue by $24,000 to $338,500. Cutting affiliate acquisition spending by $6,000 reduces costs from $224,750 to $218,750. Profit becomes $119,750, approximately 35.38%. All other lanes remain unchanged; this sensitivity does not replace the $137,750 canonical base profit.

worksheets.completion_gate: Advance when all three canonical scenarios reconcile exactly, retained affiliate commissions are separated from customer activity, acquisition allocations total correctly, and a weekly cash forecast funds operations without customer balances.

worksheets.title: End-to-End Execution, Idempotent Ledger & QA Pre-Flight Sheet
worksheets.purpose: Translate commercial terms into reliable software and accounting events. Define market-data normalization, jurisdiction-aware promotion, signed attribution callbacks, idempotent commission entries, and statement reconciliation. Establish observable failure behavior so stale quotes, duplicate callbacks, or counterparty corrections cannot silently inflate revenue.
instructions: Draw separate event paths for paid analytics access and affiliate attribution. Identify each system of record, event producer, consumer, timestamp, and financial effect; the analytics path must never become an undocumented order-routing or customer-fund processing path.

Specify deterministic identifiers and durable event storage before accepting production callbacks. Test duplicate delivery, delayed arrival, contradictory status changes, and replay; a successful HTTP response must follow durable acceptance rather than an uncommitted in-memory operation.

Replay recorded market events through the normalizer with intentionally missing sequence numbers and out-of-order timestamps. Verify that comparison features stop when source freshness or settlement mapping fails, while clearly labeled historical research remains available to subscribers.

Reconcile approved affiliate events to counterparty statements and bank receipts using distinct accrual and collection entries. Escalate mismatches by event identifier and amount; never overwrite historical entries simply to make a statement total agree with a bank deposit.

Complete a pre-production evidence packet containing test inputs, expected outcomes, actual outcomes, reviewer names, and remaining defects. Require specific remediation for age, geography, attribution, ledger, or stale-data failures before enabling the affected feature for real customers.

fields.name: End-to-end event ownership map
fields.prompt: Describe the systems traversed by a subscription purchase and an affiliate referral. Identify which system owns payment, eligibility, identity, commission approval, and accounting, while explicitly excluding venue customer funds from company custody.
fields.example: Stripe records the software subscription payment, the application grants research access, and the ledger recognizes service revenue over time. Separately, an eligible referral reaches the licensed operator, which performs account verification and handles deposits. Its signed callback reports commission status; the company never receives the user's deposit or trading instructions.

fields.name: Market event normalization contract
fields.prompt: Define normalized instrument identifiers, settlement references, bid and ask units, source timestamps, receive timestamps, and sequence numbers. Explain how adapters preserve venue-specific rules instead of erasing economically meaningful differences during normalization.
fields.example: Normalized event EV-1042 contains venue identifier, instrument identifier, settlement-rule hash, bid 46 cents, ask 48 cents, source sequence 8217, and two UTC timestamps. The adapter stores original payload bytes alongside normalized values. A changed settlement-rule hash removes the instrument from matched comparisons until an analyst approves the new mapping.

fields.name: Freshness and sequence-gap acceptance
fields.prompt: Set measurable freshness and continuity limits for each data source, including behavior during connection loss. Define when a snapshot can restore service and which user-visible information remains available while live comparisons are suspended.
fields.example: The sample service targets 500-millisecond internal processing latency and rejects live comparisons after 1,500 milliseconds of quote age. A sequence jump from 8217 to 8220 triggers snapshot recovery and disables spread alerts. Historical charts remain readable with their actual timestamps; freshness is never implied by a newly rendered page.

fields.name: Age and geographic eligibility decision
fields.prompt: Record the eligibility inputs, policy version, decision outcome, and minimal audit evidence for promotional access. Distinguish preliminary publisher screening from the licensed operator's authoritative identity and location checks before regulated participation.
fields.example: Request R-208 receives policy version 14, a 21-plus attestation, and location evidence consistent with New Jersey. The portal shows only approved New Jersey offers. A conflicting location signal removes promotional links and displays general research instead. The licensed operator still performs its required verification before accepting participation.

fields.name: Signed server-to-server callback validation
fields.prompt: Specify callback authentication, timestamp tolerance, replay handling, schema validation, and credential rotation. Describe how raw payload bytes are authenticated and how rejected callbacks are investigated without leaking personal or secret data into logs.
fields.example: The receiver verifies an HMAC-SHA256 signature over the agreed timestamp and raw request body using hmac.compare_digest. A five-minute freshness window blocks stale new requests; authenticated retries use the durable event key. Key identifiers support rotation, and logs retain event references rather than credentials, complete identities, or deposit details.

fields.name: Idempotency key and transactional persistence
fields.prompt: Define the unique business-event key and transaction boundary connecting event ingestion to ledger effects. Distinguish duplicate delivery from a genuine revision, and explain how failed processing can resume without creating duplicate commission revenue.
fields.example: The unique key combines operator account, source event identifier, event type, and source revision. A database transaction stores the accepted event and pending ledger action together. Replaying the same $300 approval twenty times leaves one $300 receivable. A later reversal receives its own linked revision and compensating entry.

fields.name: Commission recognition and collection entries
fields.prompt: Write the accounting effects for pending, approved, paid, and reversed commissions. State when entitlement becomes supportable and variable consideration sufficiently constrained; keep collection, earned revenue, and contractual reversal treatment distinct.
fields.example: A pending CPA event creates no revenue entry. An earned, sufficiently supportable $300 approval debits affiliate receivables and credits CPA revenue. Collection debits cash and credits receivables. A subsequent contractual cancellation uses a linked revenue reversal, while inability to collect an otherwise valid receivable follows the credit-loss policy.

fields.name: Statement and bank reconciliation
fields.prompt: Compare event-level accruals, counterparty statement totals, payment remittances, and bank receipts. Set a review threshold and owner for differences; preserve the distinction between withheld payment, reversed entitlement, and simple timing differences.
fields.example: The ledger shows 40 approved CPA events totaling $12,000. The statement includes 38 events and $11,400; the bank receives $11,400. Two missing identifiers create a $600 dispute, not an automatic write-off. The operations contractor requests clarification within two business days and retains the original approval evidence.

fields.name: Data minimization and retention test
fields.prompt: Specify the smallest identifiers and attributes needed for attribution and audit. Separate operational retention, accounting retention, and deletion requests; test that logs, backups, and exports do not casually replicate unnecessary customer information.
fields.example: The attribution store uses a pseudonymous click identifier, jurisdiction decision, campaign identifier, and commission event reference. It excludes payment-card data and identity-document images. A proposed 90-day raw-click retention period is reviewed against contractual and statutory needs; accounting evidence follows a separate documented schedule with restricted access.

fields.name: Pre-flight replay and defect disposition
fields.prompt: List reproducible test cases, expected results, actual evidence locations, and release-blocking defects. Include duplicate callbacks, invalid signatures, stale quotes, ineligible geography, refunds, and statement discrepancies rather than testing only successful purchases.
fields.example: The release suite contains 24 cases: eight attribution, six market-data, four eligibility, and six ledger tests. Expected results include one receivable after twenty duplicate deliveries and zero promotional links for restricted locations. Actual outcomes must be entered from execution; this example does not assert that any tests have run.

worksheets.completion_gate: Enable production features only after recorded tests demonstrate correct eligibility behavior, stale-data suppression, authenticated callbacks, exactly-once financial effects, and reconcilable commission entries. Record every untested or failed case explicitly.

worksheets.title: Statutory, Licensing, Contract Addendum & Compliance Audit
worksheets.purpose: Convert legal boundaries into specific product constraints, contract language, and evidence ownership. Review federal derivatives classifications separately from state gaming requirements and Ontario rules. Establish product-specific permissions, accurate endorsements, responsible-gaming information, and documented suspension procedures before compensated promotion begins.
instructions: Prepare a factual activity description before asking for a classification determination. Include compensation, personalization, solicitation, credentials, order handling, and money movement; publisher terminology or a non-custodial architecture alone does not resolve all CFTC registration questions.

Build a jurisdiction-by-product register using current official materials and counterparty agreements. Record which entity needs a license, registration, notification, or contractual authorization; never assume that requirements for one state, product, or compensation model transfer to another.

Negotiate objective commission definitions and inspection rights before buying traffic. Address qualifying events, deductions, payment dates, negative carryover, attribution conflicts, reversals, and termination tails; vague language about operator discretion can erase otherwise attractive cohort economics.

Review every acquisition surface for age restriction, geographic targeting, relationship disclosure, promotion accuracy, and responsible-gaming resources. Store approved versions and test rendered pages; a correct policy document cannot repair a misleading comparison page delivered to users.

Assign renewal dates, change monitoring, and suspension authority to named operating roles. When a venue's status or legal scope changes, disable affected promotion and integrations promptly while preserving records needed to reconcile already earned commissions.

fields.name: Federal derivatives classification memorandum
fields.prompt: Document the proposed activity against relevant CEA definitions and registration provisions. Ask the reviewer to address IB, FCM, and CTA considerations separately and identify the facts that would change the classification of the product.
fields.example: The review references 7 U.S.C. 1a(12), 1a(28), 1a(31), and 6d, plus 17 CFR 1.3 and 3.10 as applicable. It examines whether research is genuinely impersonal and whether compensation involves solicitation. Any reliance on CTA exclusions or 17 CFR 4.14 is supported by specific facts, not a website label.

fields.name: DCM and product-scope verification
fields.prompt: Record the venue designation evidence, specific contract category, applicable restrictions, and pending legal developments relevant to the proposed audience. Explain why venue-level designation does not eliminate product-specific or jurisdiction-specific review.
fields.example: The venue packet references 7 U.S.C. 7 and 17 CFR Part 38 for DCM status, then separately identifies the actual event contracts displayed. Sports-related contracts receive their own current jurisdictional assessment. A designated venue is not treated as automatic permission to market every listed contract everywhere.

fields.name: New Jersey and Pennsylvania requirements
fields.prompt: Identify the exact affiliate activity, compensation arrangement, regulator process, and required status in New Jersey and Pennsylvania. Attach current regulator instructions and distinguish vendor obligations from the licensed operator's own permissions.
fields.example: The New Jersey workstream checks N.J.S.A. 5:12-92 and applicable NJ DGE vendor requirements, including N.J.A.C. 13:69J where relevant. The Pennsylvania workstream separately reviews 4 Pa.C.S. Chapters 13B and 13C and PGCB instructions. Neither workstream opens until the specific activity and required status are documented.

fields.name: Michigan and West Virginia requirements
fields.prompt: Record product-specific requirements for Michigan and West Virginia, including the affiliate's role and the counterparty's authorization. Assign an evidence owner and explain how territorial controls respond to a suspended or expired status.
fields.example: Michigan review distinguishes internet gaming under MCL 432.301 et seq. from sports betting under MCL 432.401 et seq. West Virginia review separates W. Va. Code 29-22D and 29-22E. The operations owner confirms applicable supplier or affiliate requirements with current MGCB and West Virginia Lottery materials before activation.

fields.name: Ontario market and promotional controls
fields.prompt: Document the Ontario operator relationship, AGCO advertising restrictions, applicable supplier status, age threshold, and geographic targeting. Keep Canadian requirements separate from United States state registrations and explain any stricter company-wide age policy.
fields.example: Ontario review uses the Gaming Control Act, 1992, S.O. 1992, c. 24 and current AGCO internet-gaming standards. The portal checks the operator's Ontario authorization and relevant iGaming Ontario relationship. Its company-wide 21-plus policy is stricter than Ontario's 19-plus casino threshold; public bonus advertising receives separate review.

fields.name: Age, location, and responsible-gaming presentation
fields.prompt: Specify where age restrictions, territorial limitations, and current help resources appear across landing pages, comparison cards, emails, and mobile layouts. Identify who verifies jurisdiction-specific wording and how changes reach every published surface.
fields.example: Every promotional card carries the 21-plus company policy, applicable territory, and a clearly reachable responsible-gaming resource. The content owner verifies current regulator-approved helpline details for NJ, PA, MI, WV, and Ontario before publication. A monthly mobile screenshot audit confirms that disclosures remain visible without opening a separate offer.

fields.name: Affiliate material-connection disclosure
fields.prompt: Write the relationship disclosure and placement rule for ranked comparisons, editorial reviews, social posts, and email promotions. Explain how compensation affects rankings and how the presentation satisfies clear, conspicuous disclosure expectations.
fields.example: A comparison page states, 'We may receive payment when an eligible reader joins a listed operator; commercial terms do not change the published scoring method.' The disclosure appears before outbound offer links and alongside paid placements. Review uses 16 CFR 255.5, and any actual paid-ranking arrangement is described accurately.

fields.name: Commission addendum and audit rights
fields.prompt: Draft concrete commercial clauses covering earned events, deduction schedules, negative carryover, payment timing, statement detail, and dispute rights. State which provisions are negotiation requests rather than executed terms, and identify who can approve changes.
fields.example: Proposed addendum: '$300 is payable for each approved qualifying depositor; statements identify every rejection reason. NGR deductions are limited to the attached schedule. No cross-brand negative carryover applies. Undisputed amounts are due within 30 days of statement issuance.' These terms remain proposed until both authorized signatories execute them.

fields.name: Traffic restrictions and prohibited routing
fields.prompt: Specify prohibited acquisition methods and destinations, including unlicensed offshore offers and unlawful sweepstakes products. Address minors, self-excluded audiences where applicable, misleading claims, and any request to evade venue identity or location controls.
fields.example: The media agreement prohibits promotion to minors, fabricated endorsements, misleading income claims, and routing United States users to unlicensed offshore or crypto gambling venues or unlawful sweepstakes casinos. Campaigns cannot suggest bypassing location checks. An offending destination is removed immediately, and the traffic source is suspended pending investigation.

fields.name: Renewal register and change-response authority
fields.prompt: Assign ownership for registration renewals, counterparty status checks, contract changes, advertising standards, and legal developments. Define the time allowed to suspend affected functionality and the evidence required before restoring commercial activity.
fields.example: The founder owns statutory status, the operations contractor owns renewal reminders, and counsel reviews material scope changes. Reminders occur 60, 30, and 10 days before documented deadlines. A confirmed authorization lapse disables affected offers immediately; restoration requires updated evidence, product-owner confirmation, and a recorded eligibility test.

worksheets.completion_gate: Proceed only after the actual activity classification, jurisdiction requirements, executed commercial terms, current disclosures, and responsible owners are documented. Unresolved territories and products remain disabled independently of qualified analytics subscription services.

worksheets.title: Automation Pipeline, Acquisition Flywheel & Risk Fallback Tracker
worksheets.purpose: Automate repeatable information processing without automating unauthorized market access. Link licensed data ingestion, probability calculations, subscriber delivery, and eligible affiliate attribution to observable controls. Build acquisition loops around useful research while defining fallbacks for outages, budget cuts, settlement changes, and counterparty disputes.
instructions: Prioritize automation by verified workload and error reduction rather than technical novelty. Measure current manual minutes, expected run volume, exception frequency, and maintenance burden; automate stable rules first and preserve human review for changing commercial or statutory interpretations.

Use only documented, permitted data interfaces and distribution rights. Configure source-specific rate limits, backoff, and credential scopes; if a desired feed is unavailable, redesign the feature instead of scraping restricted content or implying unsupported real-time coverage.

Build the acquisition loop around original methodology, transparent comparisons, useful alerts, and subscription retention. Separate educational engagement from regulated promotional eligibility; a reader's interest in probabilities does not establish that a sportsbook offer may be displayed.

Instrument every automation with an owner, latency target, error budget, alert threshold, and recovery procedure. Test loss of a market-data source and an affiliate partner separately; a single outage should not corrupt the ledger or collapse unrelated subscriber features.

Review acquisition economics weekly and counterparty concentration monthly. Reduce spending when approved-event contribution falls below the written floor; retain subscriber service and reconciliation capacity so growth decisions do not sacrifice collection quality or existing customer trust.

fields.name: Automation backlog and labor return
fields.prompt: Rank candidate automations by hours saved, financial error prevented, implementation effort, and maintenance ownership. Include exception handling in the estimate so nominal processing speed does not conceal a growing manual-review queue.
fields.example: Monthly statement matching takes 12 hours across four counterparties. A 24-hour implementation reduces routine matching to three hours while retaining two hours for exceptions, saving seven hours monthly. The founder prioritizes this over a cosmetic dashboard because it accelerates collection and exposes missing commission events.

fields.name: Permitted feed architecture and isolation
fields.prompt: Describe ingestion adapters, message storage, normalization, and subscriber delivery for each permitted source. Document credential scope and failure isolation; avoid implying that every named venue supplies equivalent streaming or redistribution functionality.
fields.example: Separate adapters handle an authorized Kalshi stream, a contracted ForecastEx delivery channel, and licensed sportsbook odds data. Each writes immutable source events before normalization. Read-only credentials cannot place orders. A failed sportsbook adapter stops its comparisons while subscription billing, historical analytics, and other permitted feeds continue.

fields.name: Probability methodology and expected-value labels
fields.prompt: Define probability estimation, fee adjustment, calibration measurement, and uncertainty presentation. Distinguish model-implied expected value from realized profit and explain how settlement differences or incomplete outcome sets invalidate simple cross-venue calculations.
fields.example: A model estimates a 54% event probability against an illustrative all-in contract cost of $0.51, implying $0.03 expected value per $1 payout before model error. The interface labels this a model estimate, displays calibration history, and suppresses the figure when settlement mapping fails or the quote becomes stale.

fields.name: Alert delivery and subscriber preference controls
fields.prompt: Specify user-selected alert thresholds, delivery channels, duplicate suppression, frequency limits, and cancellation handling. Keep the alert service informational and explain how it avoids handling orders, customer credentials, or personalized account instructions.
fields.example: A subscriber selects a three-point probability-gap threshold and a maximum of five alerts daily. The service deduplicates by instrument, methodology version, and five-minute window. Messages link to research rather than transmitting orders. Unsubscribing stops promotional email promptly, while necessary subscription receipts remain on a separate transactional channel.

fields.name: Search and editorial acquisition loop
fields.prompt: Plan a repeatable publishing cycle that produces original, evidence-based research and measurable subscription interest. Separate editorial utility from affiliate placement and identify how published methodology, corrections, and attribution preserve credibility.
fields.example: The weekly cycle publishes one settlement-rule explainer, one probability calibration report, and one jurisdiction-specific comparison update. Each page links to a sample terminal and clearly identifies paid relationships. Acquisition reporting measures qualified trial starts and paid retention, not merely clicks sent to an operator or raw customer deposits.

fields.name: Trial conversion and subscription retention
fields.prompt: Calculate the funnel from qualified visitors to trials, paid subscribers, and retained subscribers. Use service-period cohorts and real acquisition spend; do not annualize a short promotional spike without explaining churn and seasonality assumptions.
fields.example: An illustrative month attracts 2,000 qualified research visitors, 160 trial starts, and 32 paid conversions. Visitor-to-paid conversion is 1.6%. With $750 allocated SaaS acquisition spending, new-subscriber CAC is $23.44. The cohort is tracked separately from the canonical 300 average subscribers, which also includes retained customers from earlier periods.

fields.name: Affiliate acquisition budget and contribution floor
fields.prompt: Set spend limits using approved events and collected economics rather than platform-reported registrations. Define the contribution floor, review cadence, and response to lower CPA rates or increasing rejection percentages in each eligible jurisdiction.
fields.example: The base CPA lane spends $24,000 annually for 400 approved events, or $60 per approval. At a $300 rate, contribution before shared costs is $240 per approval. A campaign is paused if trailing approved-event CAC exceeds $120 for two weekly reviews or the operator reduces its payable rate without notice.

fields.name: Outage fallback and circuit-breaker policy
fields.prompt: Define trigger thresholds, user messaging, feature degradation, recovery tests, and incident ownership for each critical dependency. Avoid substituting a second source unless its display rights and settlement semantics are independently suitable for the same feature.
fields.example: Three failed connection attempts within 60 seconds open the source circuit breaker. The terminal suppresses live comparisons and shows timestamped historical charts with an outage notice. Recovery requires a valid snapshot and continuous sequence processing for five minutes. The engineer cannot silently substitute an unlicensed odds feed to preserve a latency target.

fields.name: Counterparty dispute and negative-carryover fallback
fields.prompt: Describe how disputed deductions, withheld payments, and persistent negative carryover change promotion and forecasting. Preserve contractual collection rights while preventing fresh acquisition spending from deepening exposure to an economically impaired partner.
fields.example: A partner adds $8,000 of unsupported administration deductions to its monthly statement. Operations opens a documented dispute and removes the affected campaign from paid acquisition. Existing earned receivables remain tracked. Forecasts apply the executed agreement, but cash planning assumes delayed collection until the counterparty supplies support or resolves the discrepancy.

fields.name: Weekly observability and exception ownership
fields.prompt: List operational indicators with thresholds, owners, and escalation actions. Include feed freshness, callback rejection rates, unmatched commissions, subscription churn, and geographic suppression so technical success cannot conceal commercial or eligibility failures.
fields.example: The engineer reviews p95 processing latency below 500 milliseconds and stale-comparison suppression. Operations reviews callback authentication failures above 1% and unmatched commissions above $300. The founder reviews monthly subscriber churn above 5% and every unexpected geographic exposure. Each exception receives an owner, due date, and linked evidence of resolution.

worksheets.completion_gate: Scale acquisition only when permitted feeds, measurable subscriber utility, approved-event contribution, functioning fallbacks, and named exception owners are demonstrated. Automation must preserve eligibility decisions and ledger integrity during outages and commercial disputes.

worksheets.title: 30-Day Launch Sprint, Pod KPI Scorecard & Exit-Readiness Ledger
worksheets.purpose: Sequence a small-team launch around verifiable operating evidence rather than premature revenue claims. Assign deliverables, cash limits, and decision rights across 30 days while respecting the two-to-six-month first-deal horizon. Preserve transferable contracts, reproducible metrics, and organized records for future diligence.
instructions: Treat the first 30 days as a qualification and product-readiness sprint, not a promise of closed affiliate revenue. The canonical time to first deal is two to six months; licensing and commercial negotiations may extend beyond the sprint.

Assign one accountable owner to each deliverable while preserving the canonical team structure. Contractors can execute defined work, but the founder retains responsibility for commercial decisions, evidence completeness, cash management, and confirmation that regulated features remain within reviewed scope.

Use weekly evidence reviews to compare shipped functionality against the intended operating model. Record actual test results, counterparty responses, and budget usage; do not convert planned milestones into completed facts merely because their scheduled dates have passed.

Build the KPI scorecard from reconciled source records and clearly defined denominators. Separate revenue, contribution, owner profit, cash collections, customer activity, and product reliability; every metric should answer a specific operating question and have a named decision owner.

Prepare exit-readiness records from the start without assuming that licenses, affiliate contracts, or data rights transfer automatically. Track assignment provisions, change-of-control requirements, intellectual-property ownership, and data limitations so future diligence does not depend on reconstructing undocumented decisions.

fields.name: Days 1–7 qualification deliverables
fields.prompt: Define the first week's evidence deliverables, owners, budget ceiling, and dependencies. Prioritize activity classification, counterparty eligibility, commercial assumptions, and source rights before commissioning integrations that may require a different operating model.
fields.example: By day seven, the founder prepares the activity memorandum, three-lane revenue model, and five-jurisdiction research register. Counsel receives a $2,500 initial review authorization within the $8,000 legal allocation. The engineer inventories permitted data interfaces. Completion requires actual documents and reviewer feedback, not merely scheduled meetings or assumed affiliate acceptance.

fields.name: Days 8–14 product and ledger build
fields.prompt: Specify the smallest useful analytics release and financial-event implementation. Include permitted ingestion, stale data behavior, subscription service periods, and replay-safe attribution without adding order execution or customer-fund handling to accelerate launch.
fields.example: The engineering contractor builds one authorized feed adapter, timestamped research charts, subscription entitlements, and a durable callback inbox. The product-work budget remains capped at $10,000 for the initial scope. A recorded demonstration must show stale-quote suppression and one commission entry after repeated delivery of the same authenticated test event.

fields.name: Days 15–21 commercial and content readiness
fields.prompt: Identify commercial negotiations, editorial assets, disclosure checks, and jurisdiction tests for week three. Separate draft offers from executed permissions and explain which nonpromotional product work can continue while affiliate registration or contracting remains incomplete.
fields.example: Operations prepares two proposed affiliate addenda, six original research articles, and mobile disclosure screenshots. Promotional links remain disabled for every relationship without completed requirements. The subscription demonstration can still show permitted historical analytics. The founder records counterparty responses and unresolved terms rather than counting draft agreements as signed deals.

fields.name: Days 22–30 controlled release decision
fields.prompt: Define release evidence, permitted audience, customer-support capacity, incident response, and remaining restrictions. State which features can launch independently and which require additional statutory, contractual, or technical evidence before exposure to real users.
fields.example: A proposed 25-person analytics pilot begins only after recorded billing, data-rights, security, and stale-feed tests pass. Affiliate promotion remains off where requirements are incomplete. The founder reviews pilot support daily and preserves the $15,000 free-cash floor. Day 30 produces an evidence-based continuation decision, not a declaration that annual scorecard revenue has been achieved.

fields.name: Pod roles and capacity allocation
fields.prompt: Assign responsibilities across the canonical full-time and contractor structure. Estimate weekly capacity, escalation coverage, and separation between implementation and financial review; identify the measurable workload trigger that justifies the scaled five-person team.
fields.example: Base staffing is one full-time founder plus engineering and operations contractors. The founder owns contracts and cash, engineering owns ingestion and reliability, and operations owns content checks and reconciliation. The scaled structure adds one full-time operator and one contractor, reaching two full-time staff and three contractors only when sustained workload and contribution support expansion.

fields.name: Revenue, margin, and collection KPI scorecard
fields.prompt: Define revenue and profit metrics using earned operator amounts, not user turnover. Include collection measures and canonical annual references, with a clear distinction between actual results, annual plans, and short-period run-rate estimates.
fields.example: The scorecard tracks earned SaaS, builder, CPA, and NGR revenue separately, plus receivables aging and bank collections. Annual reference points remain $75,000 revenue and $19,500 profit; $362,500 and $137,750; and $650,000 and $325,000. Their margins are 26%, 38.0%, and 50%. Actual pilot results occupy separate entries and never inherit those planned totals.

fields.name: Service and acquisition KPI definitions
fields.prompt: Specify calculation windows, denominators, source systems, and owners for service reliability and growth metrics. Avoid vanity metrics that reward ineligible traffic or hide rejection rates, and connect each threshold to a concrete operating response.
fields.example: Approved CPA conversion equals approved FTDs divided by submitted FTD events within the same matured cohort. Subscription churn equals lost paid accounts divided by opening paid accounts for the month. Feed availability counts only periods meeting freshness requirements. The founder reviews acquisition quality weekly; engineering reviews reliability daily and documents every threshold breach.

fields.name: Exit diligence and assignment ledger
fields.prompt: List evidence a buyer would need to understand transferable revenue, intellectual property, data rights, and regulatory dependencies. Record actual assignment clauses and change-of-control requirements instead of assuming that a share sale or asset sale preserves every relationship.
fields.example: The diligence index includes executed affiliate contracts, twelve monthly reconciliations when available, contractor IP assignments, data licenses, registration records, and subscriber cohort definitions. Each contract has an assignment summary and required counterparty actions. A buyer cannot assume registrations or feed permissions transfer; unresolved transfer requirements reduce the pool of immediately portable revenue.

fields.name: Operating risk register and pause authority
fields.prompt: Rank risks by trigger, financial exposure, owner, response time, and recovery evidence. Include licensing faults, data outages, deduction disputes, seasonality, and key-person dependence; specify who can stop affected activity without waiting for a routine meeting.
fields.example: The founder can immediately suspend an affected affiliate relationship after a confirmed permission failure. Engineering can disable live comparisons after continuity loss. Operations can pause paid acquisition after an unexplained statement deduction. Each incident retains its timeline, revenue exposure, corrective action, and restoration evidence; unrelated qualified subscription service remains available where technically feasible.

fields.name: Day-30 decision and next financing milestone
fields.prompt: Record actual deliverables, remaining dependencies, cash position, and the next evidence-based spending decision. Tie continued investment to qualified demand and operating readiness while preserving the canonical two-to-six-month first-deal horizon and avoiding premature scale commitments.
fields.example: Illustrative decision: continue analytics development if the pilot has ten paying subscribers, reconciled billing, and no unresolved critical defects; keep affiliate acquisition disabled until requirements are complete. Authorize a further $3,000 only if free cash stays above $15,000. Record actual results before adopting this decision, and schedule the next commercial review in 30 days.

worksheets.completion_gate: Close the sprint only with actual deliverable evidence, a reconciled cash position, assigned unresolved dependencies, and a dated continuation decision. Preserve the exact canonical scorecard as a planning reference while reporting actual operating results separately and faithfully.
